digest.component_or_area: enrich gate marker / queue drain fast path
propositions: The enrich gate marker writes only when a full scan finds zero pending entries, causing any single pending entry to disable the O(1) fast path store-wide and force O(store-size) walks on every subsequent probe.
Measured cost on a 4,938-ticket store: one pending entry incurs 1.2–1.3 seconds per write versus 0.110 ms with the marker engaged (4,800x slowdown).

Generalized marker must record a 'live' set (ticket ids with enqueued, not-DONE entries) and scope scoped probes to O(backlog) reductions instead of full directory walks, with the TTL measured from the last full scan (scoped probes do not refresh written_ns).

Marker writes now always occur (never conditional on empty pending), validating the live field type and distrusting the whole marker on mismatch, preserving the three honesty rules: marker asserts only absence, every append still clears it, and pending verdicts come only from reducing real queue events.

The scan loop including the f400 (not_before_ns, id) service-order sort is extracted into a single _scan_pending helper called by both full-walk and scoped-walk paths to ensure result ordering parity and prevent McCabe ceiling violations.

New tests pin the standing-backlog reduction count to live-set size (independent of store size), verify TTL still bounds scoped probes, validate live-field type checking, confirm new-enqueue visibility through marker clears, and test time-driven transitions at soak deadlines and lease expiry.
